  "content": "# B-137a implementation plan\n\n## Public seams and invariant order\n\nThe behavior-facing seams are:\n1. `host_run` submit/foreground attach;\n2. `host_run_status(runId, waitMs<=30000)`;\n3. `host_run_cancel(runId, reason?)`;\n4. `cross_host_review` as the privileged verdict-profile owner;\n5. `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` plus the REVIEW gate as managed-evidence consumers.\n\nPrivate worker, file layout, launch adapters and reconciliation helpers are tested only through those seams or through real child-process effects. Each vertical slice follows RED → minimal GREEN; implementation does not bulk-create imagined internal tests.\n\n## CHK-001 — Persist and reconcile managed host-run lifecycle\n\nCreate a deep `core/managed-host-run.ts` module whose small interface owns submit, attach/status projection, cancel, worker execution and reconcile. A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.\n\nSubmit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. The hidden worker wins `claim.json` using exclusive create, validates the one-shot capability, unlinks both input files, marks `claimReady`, acquires provider admission, launches the private provider adapter and periodically advances `workerHeartbeatAt`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.\n\nA terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.\n\nInitial RED tests cover: exclusive claim winner, unchanged running state across silent intervals, worker crash followed by deadline reconciliation, one terminal under concurrent reconcilers, idempotent status/cancel, terminal/result digest stability, capability/prompt deletion, and no automatic retry.\n\n## CHK-002 — Expose submit, attach, status and cancel command surfaces\n\nExtend the host-run command schema:\n- `host_run --detach` submits, waits only for a bounded claim handshake, and returns `runId/state/deadlineAt/generation`;\n- foreground `host_run` calls the same submit path then attaches to that run, projecting live output and final usage without owning the provider child;\n- `host_run_status --runId ... --waitMs ...` performs bounded long-poll, returning immediately on terminal or snapshot-generation change and otherwise after at most 30000ms;\n- `host_run_cancel --runId ... --reason ...` writes an idempotent cooperative request and reconciles;\n- hidden `host_run_worker --runId ...` is runtime-only and never advertised as an operator workflow.\n\nDeclare command policy, process-fact level and CLI watchdog behavior for runtime continuation. A foreground caller/watchdog exit may end attachment but cannot convert the managed run to failed or cancel the worker. JSON stdout remains one machine object; text mode keeps live stream routing and concise status guidance. The handler never stores raw prompt/capability in argv or durable public artifacts.\n\nRED starts at CLI/handler seams: detach returns after claim, status wait is capped, foreground and detached share one run/receipt shape, cancel is idempotent, unknown run is fail-closed, and caller termination leaves the run queryable.\n\n## CHK-003 — Supervise provider processes portably and honestly\n\nProvider adapters remain private to ManagedHostRun and preserve canonical launcher specifications. Codex uses documented `codex exec ... -`, the worker writes the prompt to stdin and closes it. Claude and agy retain their canonical launcher contracts.\n\nOn POSIX, spawn the provider as a new process group and persist PID/PGID plus a launch fingerprint. Cancellation/deadline cleanup is TERM → bounded grace → KILL → reap → residual probe. Identity is revalidated before signals. On unsupported platforms, managed execution refuses before provider spawn with a structured unsupported-platform terminal; it does not silently degrade to child-only cleanup.\n\nMove the first-output clock to diagnostics only. Preserve finite total timeout/deadline, bounded output projection, provider usage candidate extraction, turn-failure diagnostic, passthrough-degradation honesty and failure classification. Worker heartbeat and provider progress are distinct fields.\n\nRED uses real local Node subprocesses for silent completion, descendant cleanup and TERM-resistant escalation, plus injected provider adapters for Codex argv/stdin closure, overflow and parsing.\n\n## CHK-004 — Enforce shared provider admission independent of usage-ledger mode\n\nExtract the slot registry from the ledger-gated branch into one provider-admission module. Acquisition happens before every provider spawn regardless of `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER`; usage preflight/budget/final rows remain conditional and keep existing fail-closed/append-honesty semantics. Slot ownership token, dead-PID reclaim, corrupt-meta stale backstop and token-guarded release remain unchanged.\n\nInventory production provider launch sites. Managed host_run and cross_host_review use ManagedHostRun admission. Direct Codex/Claude/Gemini leaves that cannot yet emit a managed receipt are explicitly `legacy_unmanaged` for lifecycle but still `admission_managed`; no launch site may be `admission_unmanaged`. Add a source registry/contract smoke so new direct spawn paths fail review until classified.\n\nPreserve candidate-spec per-chunk streaming, 64KiB discard-all overflow and null first-output diagnostics. RED covers ledger-off cap contention, dead/corrupt/live slot reclaim, release race, and source inventory completeness.\n\n## CHK-005 — Route cross-host review through managed execution\n\nKeep `cross_host_review` as profile owner. It still resolves the authoritative story worktree, captures clean HEAD/material/storyFiles facts, authorizes read-only Codex dispatch, creates the detached review snapshot, redacts environment, computes the existing policy timeout ceiling, constructs the structured-verdict prompt and validates the returned verdict schema.\n\nReplace only its direct provider execution with internal ManagedHostRun submit+attach using profile `cross-host-verdict` and opaque bindings. The terminal receipt is included in paired host-verdict provenance. Provider nonzero/timeout/cancel/admission refusal/invalid verdict continue to yield the existing honest blocked/error decision; no raw provider stdout becomes gate evidence.\n\nProtect configured `provider.codex`, `cross_host_review`, bounded retry and fail-closed policies with exact source/runtime regression assertions. RED captures the current direct leaf, then proves the managed path while all existing cross-host checks remain green.\n\n## CHK-006 — Bind formal reviewer evidence to exact managed receipts\n\nAdd a versioned managed-execution binding and a two-phase provider-authored evidence protocol. The profile owner seals opaque bindings at submit: storyId, reviewRunId, lane, intended provider/transport, prompt-envelope/body/context/assembled digests, materialHash, headHash and storyFilesHash. While running, the provider reviewer writes exactly one immutable proposal into the evidence journal: pass or findings plus truthful readManifest/readLog and its registered reviewer identity. It does not call final `review_pass_set` or `finding_add`.\n\nSuccessful terminal creation seals the spec digest, proposal digest and append-only journal digest. After terminal, `managed_review_evidence_import` accepts only a runId/receipt reference, reads the sealed provider-authored bytes, and imports the existing ReviewPass/Finding shape while preserving agent/lane/reviewRun/read provenance exactly. It exposes no verdict/note/finding override fields, is idempotent, and refuses non-success terminal, residual/replacement ambiguity, missing/multiple proposals or any digest mismatch. The controller may trigger import but cannot become the reviewer or reinterpret its verdict.\n\nRegister this managed receipt/composite evidence as a canonical artifact kind in shared Proof Admissibility with producer boundary, scope, REVIEW consumer, claim kind, temporal/material role, semantic field binding and canonical reason codes. Both import-time admission and the REVIEW gate must call the same shared registry/intake/evaluator; process-fact registry declares the gate semantics but is not a substitute. The gate revalidates current terminal, proposal/journal integrity, exact ReviewRun/lane/provider/prompt envelope and current material tuple instead of trusting persisted booleans.\n\nNative-host reviewer lanes retain their existing signed ReviewRun/pass/finding path and are not falsely described as mechanically supervised by ManagedHostRun. Main/implementer/controller-authored evidence, raw CLI output, usage-ledger rows, B-1be5-style time-window matching, pre-terminal proposals and structured degraded decisions cannot upgrade to normal managed receipt assurance.\n\nRED tests the valid provider proposal → successful terminal seal → importer → REVIEW gate path, plus forged runId/terminal/journal/proposal, stale/cross-story/cross-lane/cross-provider/material mismatch, raw CLI absence, controller override/self-assertion, multiple proposals, importer replay, and non-success terminal. A mutation/source-contract test proves both write-time and gate call the shared evaluator: bypassing either call or adding a parallel special-case evaluator must fail.\n\n## CHK-007 — Add adversarial coverage, observability, migration docs and rollout controls\n\nCreate an auto-discovered aggregate smoke so no package.json script is needed. It runs focused managed lifecycle, command, real process-group, admission, cross-host and receipt-gate tests. Add bounded mutation bites that prove premature silence failure, terminal-only monitoring and forged receipt changes are caught. Avoid destructive shared-dist mutations during parallel review.\n\nRegister host-run runtime artifacts with gitignore/material-hash/repair semantics. `doctor`/status diagnostics distinguish worker liveness, provider progress observability, deadline, cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. GC removes only terminal runs beyond retention; active runs and unconsumed one-shot inputs are protected, while failed startup cleanup removes secrets.\n\nUpdate `docs/host-run-usage.md` and add `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` as the durable decision truth. Document exact operator commands, 30-second wait semantics, deadline reconciliation, no silence-based restart, legacy_unmanaged vs admission_managed, the local same-uid trust ceiling, and that native subagents are out of scope.\n\nRollout is compatibility-first for non-review agent runs but enforcement is immediate for the new managed CLI-review evidence class: a raw CLI execution may still be used manually, but it cannot satisfy a formal managed reviewer gate. Final verification includes build, focused aggregate smoke, existing host-run/cross-host/provider/dispatch/review/gate suites, process/runtime registry contracts, source scans, protected timeout diff, and a real caller-detach scenario whose original run reaches terminal without a duplicate.\n"

## 2. Trigger and Observed Evidence

B-7776 was a small cleanup that removed a misleading unused parameter. The
implementation itself was correct, but its lifecycle exposed six independent
failure modes. Claude's follow-up source audit confirmed all six; it also
corrected two details in the initial diagnosis:

- the multi-minute host stall occurs during real CLI execution, not during the

- the scope-path mismatch is between checklist-relative and repo-root-relative

## 7. Workstream B — Unattended Host Liveness and Routing Specificity

### 7.1 Scope

Own C2 and C3 together because both belong to candidate proposal routing and its
host-execution boundary. This workstream does not alter cross-host quorum policy
or claim that a fake host is production evidence.

### 7.2 Host readiness and liveness

Availability, launcher compatibility, unattended readiness, first output, and
total execution are distinct states. The router must require positive unattended
readiness before automatic execution. `launcherSupport: unverified` is not
eligible for unattended routing.

Add two bounded execution controls:

- a configurable startup/first-output watchdog;
- a total host execution deadline.

The first-output watchdog must account for known launchers that legitimately
delay output, and its timeout must produce a launcher/auth/interactive/no-output
diagnostic rather than a generic disagreement. Both controls must propagate
abort to `host_run`, kill the child, and release capacity.

`host=fake` is allowed only in deterministic tests or explicit local diagnostics.
It must never be suggested as a production assurance substitute.

### 7.3 Query specificity

Add corpus document-frequency/IDF information to deterministic query selection.
Generic tokens above a configurable frequency threshold may be removed or
down-weighted. A 40% threshold is a candidate rollout value, not a permanent
unexplained constant.

Frequency filtering must never suppress:

- explicit `relatedDocs`;
- exact file paths or semantic anchors;
  earlier actionable diagnosis and fragments from different streams can never
  combine into a false diagnosis;
- the existing `maxDocumentFrequencyRatio` filter remains authoritative.
  Document-frequency filtering occurs before the query-group budget is spent,
  so generic or zero-hit groups cannot starve a later matching specific term;
  overbroad and zero-hit terms remain typed in signed audit metrics.
  Truncation artifacts now record query group, retained/omitted counts, omitted
  maximum score, and selected cutoff; raw overflow escalates only when an
  omitted candidate can enter or tie the bounded selection;
- direct candidates use explicit typed sources (`related-doc`, exact path,
  registry reference, path-bearing structured risk, or `filesReadFully` from
  current signed reviewer evidence). Filename-only triage is never promoted.
  Existing safe repo-relative files outside the requirements corpus receive a
  content hash and remain mandatory; unsafe/missing/non-file paths produce a
  typed diagnostic. Mandatory candidates are retained before the ordinary
  candidate budget and may exceed it without silent loss. Cutoff/tie decisions
  are computed only from ordinary ranking, so a protected-only route does not
  escalate because mandatory count exceeds the ordinary budget. Generic
  structured auth/production risks may escalate but do not fabricate a path;
  a structured signal protects a source only when it resolves to an existing
  exact repo-relative path or a declared canonical registry/source mapping. Story title,
  description, and checklist prose remain ordinary search seeds and cannot
  trigger typed-risk escalation;
- the signed artifact carries `mode`, while the candidate/reason projection is
  identical across shadow, warn, and enforce. Renderer, reviewer dispatch, and
  read-binding consumers detect mode disagreement for story-level and actual
  item-scoped dispatch. Diagnostics are separate from blocking errors: shadow
  records, warn advises with an owner next action, and enforce rejects;
- when every usable query term is filtered as generic, routing records a bounded
  generic-only disposition rather than manufacturing `zero_candidates` or a
  full-corpus escalation. Raw-hit truncation compares omitted relevance against
  the ordinary (non-mandatory) selected cutoff.

Deterministic smoke coverage uses injected readiness rows, a minimal child/timer
seam for explicit output/timeout/error/abort race schedules, and local Node child
processes only; it asserts settle-once, kill-at-most-once, timer/listener cleanup,
and capacity reacquisition, and never launches Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, or Antigravity CLI.
The readiness probe remains the existing bounded synchronous classifier; this
work does not redesign probe scheduling or change quorum/production authority.
Startup/total watchdog defaults are enabled for automatic candidate proposals;
other `host_run` callers remain backward-compatible opt-in consumers.
